evals.prompt: Create UI mocks for a desktop team-members screen. Every variant must show the same title, a search field, an Invite member button, and a table with Name, Role, and Status columns. Use these rows: Ana / Owner / Active; Dev / Viewer / Invited. I want to choose a visual direction.
evals.expected_output: One self-contained HTML comparison containing three genuinely different, fully styled static UI directions. The variants are stacked, visibly labeled A, B, and C, preserve identical requirements and data, and contain no descriptive substitute for rendered UI.
expectations: Renders three actual styled UI mocks rather than descriptions, feature lists, or annotated placeholders.
Stacks the variants in alphabetical order and labels them visibly as A, B, and C without direction names or rationale.
Preserves the same title, search field, Invite member button, columns, and supplied rows in every variant.
Makes the variants meaningfully different design or layout directions rather than cosmetic color, type, or spacing changes.
Keeps the comparison usable at narrow and desktop widths and verifies it for clipping, horizontal page overflow, and ambiguous labels.

evals.prompt: Create four static mobile checkout UI mock variants and lay them out side by side. Each must show Order summary, Shipping address, Payment method, a total of $84.00, and a Place order button. Label the options for selection and do not include design commentary.
evals.expected_output: One self-contained HTML comparison containing four equally sized mobile mock surfaces arranged side by side as explicitly requested and labeled A through D. Each is a distinct rendered design direction with identical supplied checkout content and no rationale or application behavior.
expectations: Honors the requested count and labels the rendered variants A, B, C, and D.
Uses the requested side-by-side comparison instead of the default stacked layout.
Preserves every supplied checkout element and the $84.00 total in all four variants.
Shows actual styled mobile UI with meaningful design differences and no variant names, rationale, or descriptive prose.
Keeps the containing page usable without silently changing the mobile target viewport.

evals.prompt: Create three static desktop UI mock directions for a Kubernetes operations overview. Every variant must show cluster health, deployment status, pod restarts, and recent alerts using the same sample data. I want bold, useful options that feel specific to platform engineers rather than default SaaS dashboard templates. Do not include design commentary.
evals.expected_output: One self-contained HTML comparison containing three polished, structurally distinct operations interfaces. Each direction is grounded in the platform-engineering subject, has a coherent identity and a controlled visual risk, preserves identical operational data, and avoids decorative AI defaults that do not support the concept.
expectations: Renders three complete desktop UI mocks labeled A, B, and C with identical cluster health, deployment status, pod restart, and recent alert data.
Explores meaningfully different information hierarchies and compositions instead of recoloring one generic dashboard shell.
Uses platform-engineering concepts and workflows to shape each direction rather than relying on unrelated trend labels or decorative motifs.
Keeps each direction visually coherent, with one controlled signature idea and no arbitrary gradients, glows, labels, colors, or repeated rounded cards.
Visually inspects the rendered comparison, fixes the largest composition and polish gaps, removes elements that add no information or identity, and verifies narrow-page containment.

evals.prompt: Create three static desktop UI mock variants for a file-import screen. Every variant must show one file being processed at 62%, a Cancel button, and a clear processing state. Use subtle animation to make progress easy to understand, but do not use video or add application behavior.
evals.expected_output: One self-contained HTML comparison with three complete file-import mocks. Motion uses lightweight CSS or inline SVG, supports reduced motion, keeps the processing state clear when animation is disabled, and avoids decorative continuous repainting.
expectations: Shows the same file, 62% progress, Cancel button, and processing state in all three variants.
Uses purposeful CSS or inline SVG motion instead of video, runtime dependencies, or application logic.
Provides a reduced-motion treatment and keeps progress understandable when animation is disabled.
Avoids large continuously repainting effects and does not add unrelated ambient animation.
Renders and checks the animated and reduced-motion states for clipping, clarity, and consistent comparison.
